title: First Response Playbook and Runbook Pruning Guidelines
author: Samira Patel
body:
Summary:
This document provides a consolidated, SLO-driven first response playbook and a practical lifecycle for runbook pruning. It covers: immediate triage and containment steps, runbook ownership and pruning cadence, on-call rotation guidance, game day (simulation) templates, postmortem minimums, and customer status page / comms templates by severity. The goal is to reduce cognitive load on responders, keep runbooks accurate, and standardize customer communication so SLAs and trust are preserved.

Audience and scope:
- Primary audience: on-call engineers, SREs, incident commanders, support leads, and engineering managers.
- Scope: covers production-facing services managed by Redwood Inference, including the serving runtime, routing, and observability layers. Not intended for low-level dev/debug notes or external compliance artifacts.

Quick reference (TL;DR):
1) First responder actions: acknowledge (within 5m), declare impact tier, limit blast radius, set bridge, notify stakeholders.
2) Escalation window: if no mitigation in 15m escalate to senior on-call; 30m to oncall lead.
3) Runbook pruning: review every 90 days; full audit annually.
4) Game day cadence: quarterly critical-path simulations plus monthly tabletop for high-risk services.

1) Incident lifecycle and first-response checklist
- Phase 0: Alerting and acknowledgement
  - Acknowledge alert within 5 minutes.
  - Attach the alert ID and link to the service dashboard in the incident ticket (PagerDuty/Incidents).
  - Record: initial symptoms, first-observed timestamp, initial SLO signal (error rate, latency p95, capacity alerts).

- Phase 1: Triage and impact classification
  1. Confirm scope: which regions, routes, and customer tiers are affected.
  2. Classify impact tier using SLO thresholds:
     - Tier P1 (SEV-1): customer-visible outage or SLO breach > 5% error budget consumed in 5m window OR > 50% users affected.
     - Tier P2 (SEV-2): degraded service with meaningful user impact and progressive SLO risk.
     - Tier P3 (SEV-3): localized/low-impact anomalies, no immediate SLO breach.
  3. Assign Incident Commander (IC). IC must be named in the ticket and take ownership within 10 minutes for P1/P2.

- Phase 2: Containment and mitigation
  - Limit blast radius (route blackhole, scale down offending model variants, shift traffic to fallback model or region).
  - If mitigation changes state (e.g., rollback, model pin), add an explicit rollback checklist item to the ticket.
  - Preserve logs and traces for the pre-mitigation window: set a retention tag for 48 hours longer than default for affected services.

- Phase 3: Communication and status updates
  - IC posts to internal incident bridge every 15 minutes for P1 until restoration, every 30 minutes for P2.
  - Use the status page templates (see section 6) for customer-facing updates.

- Phase 4: Recovery and verification
  - Confirm SLOs returning to normal over a 30-minute rolling window.
  - Validate with a smoke test: a set of automated queries (sample prompts) that exercise affected endpoints.
  - Once verified, move to Postmortem planning.

2) Ownership, escalation, and contact matrix
- Owners:
  - Service owner: the product/engineer team responsible for the service. Responsible for runbook accuracy and post-incident remediation.
  - On-call engineer: first responder; executes runbook steps and documents actions.
  - Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, authorises comms, decides rollback or mitigations.
  - SRE lead: second-line escalation; assists with capacity/infra changes.

- Escalation windows and triggers:
  - 0–5 minutes: first on-call acknowledges.
  - 5–15 minutes: if no mitigation progress, escalate to senior on-call.
  - 30 minutes: oncall lead notified; consider bridge-level stakeholder notifications and customer-impact declaration.
  - Immediate escalation to executive updates if outage projected > 2 hours or strategic customers affected.

3) Runbook lifecycle and pruning guidelines
- Motivation: outdated runbooks are harmful. Pruning keeps instructions short, verified, and effective under stress.

- Runbook format requirements (per-runbook header table):
  - Service name: short tag
  - Owner: team + primary contact (PagerDuty ID)
  - Last tested: YYYY-MM-DD
  - Priority: P1/P2/P3
  - Runbook version: semantic version (v1.2.0)

- Minimum contents for a valid runbook:
  1. Clear purpose and scope (1–2 sentences).
  2. Preconditions and safe-to-run checks (read-only checks, impact indicators).
  3. Step-by-step mitigation instructions (concise commands/URLs).
  4. Post-mitigation verification steps.
  5. Rollback instructions and known side effects.
  6. Contact and escalation list (names, roles, PD aliases).

- Pruning cadence and process:
  - Automatic reminders: Runbook owners receive a scheduled review reminder 90 days after last tested.
  - Quick prune (90-day): Owner checks that top 3 steps are still correct, updates 'last tested'.
  - Deep audit (annual): cross-team verification, runbook test in a sandboxed game day, and update version.
  - Decommission: if a runbook is unused for 12 months and the service has been retired, archive and tag as 'deprecated'.

- Pruning checklist (owners must sign off):
  - Execute or validate the first three steps in a non-prod environment.
  - Verify associated dashboards and alert queries are still valid.
  - Replace any stale CLI commands or hard-coded resource names.
  - Reduce instructions to no more than 12 discrete steps for P1 actions.

4) On-call rotation guidance and handoffs
- Rotation types:
  - Primary on-call (service-specific): 1 week duration recommended.
  - Secondary on-call (cross-service backup): 2-week staggered rotation to provide continuity.
  - On-call lead (monthly): available for escalations and coaching.

- Handoff checklist (to be completed at rotation day change):
  1. Post active incidents and outstanding action items to the rotation board.
  2. Ensure runbook 'last tested' is visible on the rotation dashboard.
  3. Confirm calendar coverage and escalation policies are current.
  4. Shadow handoff: outgoing and incoming on-call do a 30-minute overlap once per rotation cycle.

- Burnout mitigations and rules of engagement:
  - Maximum consecutive primary weeks: 2.
  - Mandatory recovery day: first weekday after a primary on-call week.
  - Swap window: allow swaps up to 48 hours before rotation start with manager approval.

5) Game days and simulation playbook
- Objectives: validate runbooks, test cross-team collaboration, and verify SLO detection paths.

- Cadence and types:
  - Quarterly critical-path full-sim: inject a realistic combined failure (e.g., multi-region model cache corruption + routing flaps).
  - Monthly tabletop: 60-minute scenario review for high-risk services.
  - Ad-hoc mini-sims: triggered after a high-severity incident to validate new mitigations.

- Typical game day run sequence (3-hour full-sim):
  1. Pre-brief and roles (15 min): IC, observers, communication lead, smoke-test owner.
  2. Injection window (30–45 min): execute fault injection in staging or a dedicated sandbox.
  3. Response and containment (60 min): runbooks executed, alternatives evaluated.
  4. Recovery verification (30 min): smoke tests and SLO checks.
  5. Debrief and action logging (30 min): capture remediation tasks, update runbooks.

- Scenarios catalog (example entries):
  - Scenario A: Model quantization regression causing silent accuracy drift and increased retries.
  - Scenario B: Routing region failover with KV cache thrash.
  - Scenario C: Auth token rotation failure impacting private deployments.

6) Status page and customer comms templates
- Principles: be truthful, timely, actionable, and consistent. Avoid technical jargon for customer-facing messages.

- Template: Initial acknowledgement (public status page)
  - Title: We are investigating increased inference latency in US-West
  - Timestamp: 2026-02-10T12:03Z
  - Impact: Some customers may experience delayed responses from the Redwood hosted inference API.
  - What we are doing: Our engineering team has identified an abnormal backend latency pattern and is actively rolling traffic away from the affected capacity pool.
  - Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner.

- Template: Mitigation in progress (status page update)
  - Title: Traffic shifted to fallback pool; mitigation in progress
  - Timestamp: 2026-02-10T12:33Z
  - Impact: Reduced latency for most customers; a small subset may still see elevated response times.
  - What we are doing: Continuing throttled rollouts and monitoring SLO metrics.
  - What you can do: Retry requests or reduce concurrency for short burst workloads.
  - Next update: in 15 minutes.

- Template: Resolved and next steps (status page final update)
  - Title: Service restored; post-incident review underway
  - Timestamp: 2026-02-10T13:10Z
  - Impact: Service restored to normal.
  - What we did: Shifted traffic to fallback pool and applied a partial rollback of the latest model variant.
  - Follow-up: A postmortem will be published within 72 hours with remediation actions.

- Direct customer notification (high-touch customers)
  - Subject: Incident report: [Service] outage on [date] - immediate actions and next steps
  - Body bullets: timeline summary, customer impact, mitigation actions taken, known residual effects, SLA/credits if applicable, contact for follow-up.

7) Postmortem and remediation requirements
- Minimum postmortem timeline:
  - Draft within 72 hours of incident resolution.
  - Owner assigns remediation tickets within 7 calendar days.
  - Final postmortem and remediation status published within 30 days.

- Postmortem template (minimum sections):
  1. Summary (one paragraph).
  2. Timeline (annotated with timestamps).
  3. Root cause analysis (contributing factors).
  4. Detection and response evaluation (what worked/what didn't).
  5. Action items (owner, due date, risk level).
  6. Runbook updates (link to updated runbook).
  7. Preventative measures and verification plan.

- Remediation ownership rules:
  - At least one action must be assigned to the service owner.
  - Short-term fixes (<= 14 days) should have a named owner and acceptance criteria.
  - Long-term mitigations (> 14 days) require architecture review and sign-off from the SRE lead.

8) Automation and tooling suggestions
- Standardize incident ticket template in PagerDuty/Incidents with required fields (impact tier, IC, affected services, SLO signals).
- Provide a single-click "start smoke tests" dashboard that runs the canonical verification queries for each service.
- Maintain a Runbook Registry (searchable index) with last-tested metadata surfaced in the on-call dashboard.

9) Training and qualification for responders
- New on-call engineers must complete:
  - Runbook reading and shadowing: 3 shadowed incidents or 2 sandbox game days.
  - Runbook execution test: complete the first three steps of a P1 runbook in a staging environment under observation.

- Certification: engineers qualify as "Responder I" after 3 months and "Responder II" after 9 months with documented simulations.

Appendices
A. Example runbook header (text table)
| Field | Value |
| Service name | inference-router |
| Owner | runtime-team (pager: runtime-oncall) |
| Last tested | 2026-01-20 |
| Priority | P1 |
| Runbook version | v1.3.0 |

B. Sample postmortem action item table (text)
- Action: Update model rollout guardrails
  - Owner: Sarah Kim
  - Due: 2026-03-05
  - Notes: Add automatic rollback at 10% sustained error increase for 10 minutes.

C. Contact shortcuts and commands
- View current on-call: /incidents oncall status
- Start bridge: /bridge start --incident $INC_ID
- Run smoke tests: /smoketest run --service inference-router

Document governance and change log:
- This page is owned by the SRE guild. Minor edits (typo fixes, clarifications) may be made by runbook owners with a short edit note. Major changes (cadence, escalation policies, or template revisions) require reviewer approval listed above.
- Change log:
  - 2024-11-12: Created by Samira Patel.
  - 2025-06-02: Added pruning cadence and onboarding checklist (reviewers: Ravi Menon).
  - 2026-02-10: Expanded status page templates and hardened escalation windows (reviewers: Evelyn Cho, Diego Alvarez).
